chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn Abdillah narrated from Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Ṭayālisī, from Al-Ḥasan ibn Alī, from his father, from Faḍl ibn Uthmān Al-Ṣāyigh, from Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār, who said:

I asked Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What should I say when I visit the grave of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'Say: Peace be upon you, O Abā 'Abdillāh. May Allāh's blessing be upon you, O Abā 'Abdillāh. May Allāh have mercy on you, O Abā 'Abdillāh. May Allāh curse those who killed you, and may Allāh curse those who participated in shedding your blood, and may Allāh curse those who heard of it and were pleased with it. Indeed, we are free from that before Allāh.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.قَبْرُ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Husayn ibn Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when visiting the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the foundational liturgy for visiting the grave of Imām al-Ḥusayn (a.s.), emphasizing not just greeting but also *tawallī* (affiliation) and *tabarrī* (dissociation) from his enemies. The specific invocation of curses upon those who were pleased with his death (*man balaghahu dhalika fa raḍiya bihi*) highlights the theological significance of emotional and spiritual alignment with the Ahl al-Bayt, a core tenet of Shia piety. This formula serves as a concise summary of the Imam’s status and the community’s relationship to his martyrdom.
